title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 53
paragraphs: Having spoken thus and having sent Artabanus back to Susa, Xerxes next summoned before him the most distinguished men of the Persians, and when they had come, he said: “Persians, I have assembled you because I want you to show yourselves good men and not to disgrace what was done in former times by the Persians, which is great and glorious. Let each of us individually, and all of us together, be zealous in our enterprise — for what we are laboring for is a common good for all. I urge you, moreover, to press on in the war without slackening your efforts, for as I am told we are marching against brave men, and if we defeat them there will be no other army of men that will ever stand against us. So now let us begin the crossing, having first prayed to those gods who have the Persians for their allotted care.”
